thread:
carmen: quick thread — throwing a new idea out: instead of per-tenant independent autotune, what if we harmonize thresholds across similar tenants to reduce noisy fanout? thinking cluster tenants by baseline and apply staggered rollout windows. thoughts? :thinking:

yusuf: interesting. pros: fewer distinct threshold flips -> less notify churn. cons: risk of grouping dissimilar workloads and masking regressions for some tenants. need strong similarity metric.

emily: agree with yusuf. similarity could be feature vector: baseline_p95, traffic_qps, region, model_type. cluster with kmeans or agglomerative. then derive cluster_proposal and map back to tenants with confidence score. low-confidence tenants fallback to org-default.

carmen: yeah, cluster_proposal = cluster_ewma + alpha * cluster_std. per-tenant effective = cluster_proposal * (1 - blend_factor) + tenant_baseline * blend_factor. blend_factor = f(confidence, sample_count). default blend_factor=0.3 so tenant gets some individual weight.

yusuf: NIT: ensure small-traffic tenants don't pull cluster away — weight samples by sample_count when computing cluster stats. also cap maximum cluster_size to avoid huge cross-tenant coupling.

emily: rollout concerns: applying cluster-based thresholds could still cause mass-change if many clusters update simultaneously. add stagger windows and a random jitter when writing effective thresholds. and global smoother token-bucket as usual.

carmen: here's a compact RFC snippet for the pipeline and knobs:

```yaml
harmonize:
  enabled: true
  cluster_features: [p95_baseline_ms, qps, region, model_type]
  clustering_algo: kmeans
  k: 20
  sample_weight_floor: 10
  blend_factor_default: 0.3
  alpha: 1.4
  cluster_max_delta_ms: 200
  per_tenant_min_samples: 50
  stagger_window_minutes: 30
  apply_jitter_seconds: 120
  global_smoother:
    tokens_per_hour: 10000
    min_apply_cost: 5
```

yusuf: also add an explainability field so console shows "why this tenant was assigned to cluster X" and a confidence score. ops will want to reject cluster applies per-org.

emily: telemetry we need: cluster_assignments_ts, cluster_proposal_ts, per_tenant_blend_factor, applied_vs_proposed_delta, cluster_size_histogram, fallback_count. and a simulator that replays last 90 days to estimate notify_delta when harmonized.

carmen: good call. i want a UX in console: list tenants in cluster, per-tenant toggle to opt-out, and a cluster-level "propose/approve" flow with audit_reason. UI should show estimated cost savings (reduced fanout) and risk metrics.

yusuf: policy question: should cluster-based harmonize be opt-in per-org by default or opt-out? my vote: opt-in for now, since it's more aggressive than per-tenant autotune.

emily: agree opt-in. we can surface recommended clusters for orgs with many small tenants where signal is weak. also add safety: if cluster fallback fraction > 10% pause and alert product.

slo-bot: started simulation: harmonize-sim-3177771000 cohort=6% duration=48h. results will include estimated_notify_delta and cluster_risk_report.

deploy-bot: scheduled shadow-run harmonize-shadow-3177772000 and canary window 3177850000-3177853600.

carmen: ok next steps: emily to prototype clustering + simulator, yusuf to draft config + API contract, i'll draft console mocks and RFC. plan: sim 48h -> shadow 72h -> staged canary with per-org opt-in. tagging @yusuf @emily for review. :thumbsup:

yusuf: +1

emily: +1, starting prototype now.
